blocks.headline: One rule. Every pair.
blocks.subtitle: Understand NumPy broadcasting by following the numbers.

blocks.text: Broadcasting lets NumPy combine arrays of different shapes without loops. It compares the two shapes **from the right**. Two sizes fit together when they are equal or when one of them is 1.
The four steps as still images
These images show the end of each animation step. They work without 3D and are easy to compare side by side.

items.caption: **2. Align.** Read the shapes from the right. Every pair is equal or contains a 1.
**3. Expand.** The pale blocks are the same stored numbers, read again.
**4. Add.** Cell [i, j, k] is A[i, 0, k] + B[0, j, 0]. The result has 24 numbers.

blocks.text: NumPy compares shapes starting from the rightmost axis. Sizes are compatible when they are equal or when one of them is 1. Missing axes on the left count as size 1.

blocks.caption: Shape alignment for this example: (2, 1, 3) with (1, 4, 1) gives (2, 4, 3)

blocks.text: A size of 1 "stretches" in a conceptual way. NumPy does not copy the data. It reads the same numbers again for each position.
blocks.title: No copy is made

items: Write the two shapes and align them on the right. Add leading 1s to the shorter shape.
For each pair of sizes: equal sizes match. A size of 1 stretches to the other size. Any other pair is an error.
The result shape takes the larger size of each pair.

blocks.text: Change the sizes of A and B in this 2D version. Step through the rule. Select an output cell in the last step to see which cell of A and which cell of B it reads.

rows: Every pair has a 1 or equal sizes
A column plus a row gives a grid

blocks.text: If both shapes are `(n, d)` with the same `n` and `d`, the operation is element by element. No axis is stretched. This is the case where a missing axis can hide a mistake.

items: Adding a bias vector `(d,)` to a batch `(n, d)`.
Scaling each column by a vector.
All pairs of rows: `x[:, None, :] - y[None, :, :]` (question [[q:30|030]]).
Gradients of broadcast values must be summed back to the original shape (question [[q:108|108]]).
